subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@atlas-payments.com>; Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on scope. Per our discussion, I’m capturing the proposed success criteria, evaluation plan, owners, and next steps so we can lock the POC timeline. Please review and confirm priorities or edits.

High-level goal: Validate Redwood inference can meet Atlas Payments’ latency, throughput, cost, and quality requirements for the fraud-screening enrichment endpoint.

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (POC):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency < 250 ms for 1–2k token context (measured from request to first-token).
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s with 50% CPU/GPU headroom during peak test windows.
- Cost: inference cost <= $0.0005 per token (target; account-level cost model to be measured).
- Quality: classification/labeling accuracy >= 92% on agreed evaluation set; human relevance score >= 4/5 on 100 sampled responses.
- Reliability: 99.9% success rate (no errors) during test windows; graceful fallback to smaller model if capacity constrained.

Evaluation plan / tests:
1) Functional smoke tests (day 1) — run on sample data to validate integration and logs. Owner: Marissa.
2) Latency & throughput runs (days 2–4) — load tests at steady-state and ramp tests to 200 req/s. Owner: Marissa.
3) Cost modeling (days 2–7) — run representative workload, capture token counts and cost. Owner: Jordan.
4) Quality eval (days 3–10) — run batch eval on annotated holdout; human review of 100 samples. Owner: Atlas + Redwood (Priya / Marissa).
5) Security/compliance checkpoint — confirm data handling and SOC2 evidence needed. Owner: Alex / Jordan.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0: kick-off & environment access (this week)
- Week 1: integration + smoke tests
- Week 2: load tests + cost runs + quality eval start
- Week 3: final sweep, results review, and decision meeting

Deliverables: POC-eval-plan-v1.xlsx (attached), test logs, cost breakdown, evaluation report, and recommended config for production.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Atlas: confirm the priority ranking for the 4 KPIs above and grant test data access (S3 sample or similar).
- Atlas: share any required security questionnaire items up front (we’ll coordinate with our security team).
- Redwood: schedule load-test windows and share test-account credentials.

I’ll put a calendar invite for Monday to kick off if that works.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — next steps

Jordan — thanks for the write-up, this is helpful and matches what we discussed. A few notes from our side:

1) KPI priorities: Quality > Latency > Reliability > Cost. If we have to trade, prioritize accuracy and relevance first.
2) Quality target: can we make the quality metric more concrete? For us that means: false positive rate < 3% on the labeled eval set and mean relevance >= 4/5 across the sampled responses.
3) Autoscaling test: we’d like to include a burst/scale test to simulate holiday traffic — can Redwood run a 10x burst scenario and confirm model warm-up times?
4) Security: we’ll send our security questionnaire (you can expect it today). We’ll need SOC2 evidence + encryption-at-rest confirmation.
5) Data: attaching a small data-sample.csv (synthetic) you can use for the early smoke tests. Full S3 access will follow after our legal review.

Timeline: we’re fine with a 3-week POC but would prefer the decision meeting in Week 2 if quality signals are strong.

I’ll coordinate with Priya and Samir on handing off the data and scheduling the burst test.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering | Atlas Payments

Thanks Alex — noted on priority order and the more specific quality metrics. Jordan: I’ll own the latency & throughput runs and the autoscaling burst test. Proposed concrete test plan:

- Day 1 (kickoff): run smoke tests using data-sample.csv — verify integration and log collection.
- Day 2: baseline latency runs at 50/100/200 req/s for steady-state p95 measurement.
- Day 3: burst test (2x, 5x, 10x) to capture warm-up and cold-start behavior; measure p50/p95/p99 and error rates.

I’ll log results in the Drive folder and flag any regressions. Jordan — I’ll need test credentials and the Drive link to push logs. Lauren — can you prep the load test schedule (windows in PST) and a short playbook for fallbacks?

Also tagging security: once we get Atlas’ questionnaire, I’ll loop in our security lead and add the SOC2 artifacts to the shared folder.

Marissa
